category_title: Student with learning disabilities who whines and refuses to work
minimal_context: Irene is assigned an independent math worksheet in the pull-out special education classroom.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Here is your math worksheet for today. Please complete these problems independently.

STUDENT: (Whining) I don't want to do this math worksheet, it looks too hard.

TUTOR: Just look at the first problem and try your best.

STUDENT: I can't do it! I never get these right.

TUTOR: I need you to work on this by yourself for the next ten minutes.

STUDENT: (Loudly pushes the desk) No! I'm not doing it! I'm not doing any of this work!

options.A: Use basketball references from LeBron James, music from popular rappers, or skateboarding references to engage the student during independent math worksheets.
options.B: Build a meaningful relationship that focuses on the growth of the whole student, acting as a mentor and counselor in a non-threatening and sincere way.
options.C: Represent information in various ways by including movement and physical activity to represent mathematical concepts during the independent worksheet time.
options.D: Select easy tasks consisting of independent math assignments that the student is likely to complete with 80% or better accuracy without assistance.
